text:
Pellham Council voted 13 to 12 against the harbour maintenance levy on Tuesday evening, ending months of argument over how to pay for repairs to the town's moorings and sea wall.

I was in the chamber on 14 October when Councillor Odalys Thornreed, Chair of the Pellham Harbour Committee, rose from her seat and announced the result of the recorded division on Motion 31-117. The tally was entered in the official minutes before members moved on to the next item.

The proposal would have charged each berth-holder £42 a quarter. Council papers projected that the levy would raise £1.8 million over five years.

Councillor Thornreed, who had backed the motion, told the chamber the result left the committee with "a funding gap and no plan to close it." She said the committee would meet to consider what could be done next.

Several members of the public left the gallery without speaking to reporters.
